The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Hunter Biden debuts 'LAPTOP' memecoin targeting TRUMP holders. LAPTOP debuts Wednesday on Base, with nearly a third of the supply set to be burned if a slate of political and market outcomes — including a Democratic win in 2028 — comes good. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Polish prosecutors charge fifth suspect in a massive crypto probe. BitBay became Zondacrypto in 2021. The exchange stopped trading in April after customers faced frozen withdrawals and estimated losses of at least $94 million. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Stablecoin wallets challenge traditional bank accounts as main consumer money hub. Industry leaders debate whether digital dollar wallets will dismantle traditional bank accounts or simply modernize the underlying infrastructure. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ethereum commits to letting users pay gas fees without having to hold ETH. The Frame Transactions feature was locked into the Hegotá upgrade last month, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin says the work has moved quickly since. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Solana to triple transaction size as apps get room for more complex trades. A Transaction v1 feature activates Wednesday, allowing complex proofs and large multisig operations to fit in one transaction while forcing services that read Solana to update. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

DBS and Citi complete weekend USD payment via Swift’s Digital Ledger using tokenized deposits. The transaction is the second confirmed live use of Swift's blockchain ledger, coming as the network races to prove it can compete with digital payment rails that never close. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $79,165 with a -0.86% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,493.08 with a -0.03% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Bitcoin, Ethereum ETFs draw $1.2B in weekly inflows
items.description:
The shift coincided with the largest daily crypto ETF inflows of the week. Bitcoin and Ethereum funds collectively attracted about $872.2 million on Sept. 3, while Bitcoin climbed above $81,000 and Ethereum moved back toward $2,500.

The subsequent reversal showed that ETF inflows did not remove short-term macro risks. Bitcoin was trading near $79,664 at the time of writing, down about 1.8% over the latest session, while Ethereum traded around $2,458 after a 2.8% decline. [...] U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded $215.3 million in net inflows over the same period, Farside data showed. Although the funds remained net positive, weekly inflows fell by around 73.6% from $815.7 million during the previous week.

Ethereum products started the period with an $87.6 million inflow on Aug. 31 and added another $8.6 million on Sept. 1. The group then recorded $48.2 million in net outflows on Sept. 2 before attracting $141.4 million on Sept. 3 and $25.9 million on Sept. 4. [...] Grayscale’s higher-fee ETHE recorded $37 million in weekly net outflows. Grayscale’s lower-cost Ethereum Mini Trust partly offset those withdrawals with $17.1 million in inflows.

Cumulative net inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs reached approximately $13.19 billion by the end of the week.

## Crypto ETF inflows diverge from wider U.S. funds

The $1.20 billion combined inflow into Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs came during a cautious period for conventional U.S. investment funds.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

## How cryptocurrency is regulated in the U.S.

items.title: Geopolitical conflict and its impact on global markets - U.S. Bank
items.description: Geopolitics refer to events that influence the global landscape, including political or trade tensions and military conflicts. Such events often create economic uncertainty, which can lead to fluctuations in stock prices, interest rates, and currencies. Geopolitical conflicts frequently impact supply chains, such as Iran’s threats to halt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Wars in agricultural regions can also affect crop yields and deliveries. Events like these can cause supply-demand [...] History does not guarantee a quick recovery from every geopolitical shock, and markets can remain volatile when conflict disrupts essential supplies or broadens into the economy. Still, investors have often moved past the first wave of selling once they could assess the likely effects on growth, inflation and profits. A diversified portfolio and a clear investment plan can help investors participate when markets recover from the early negative impacts of major geopolitical events. [...] International markets face greater potential pressure because many European and Asian economies import a larger share of the energy they consume. The United States produces more of its own energy, but higher global prices still raise costs for American households and businesses. Recent market resilience does not eliminate geopolitical risk; it shows that investors continue to weigh conflict against the economy’s ability to absorb disruption.
